<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Rishi Jha
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Collin Zhang
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Vitaly Shmatikov
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">John X. Morris
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Department of Computer Science
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Cornell University
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce the first method for translating text embeddings from one vector space to another without any paired data, encoders, or predefined sets of matches. Our unsupervised approach translates any embedding to and from a universal latent representation (i.e., a universal semantic structure conjectured by the Platonic Representation Hypothesis). Our translations achieve high cosine similarity across model pairs with different architectures, parameter counts, and training datasets.</p>
    
<p id="abstract1.2" class="ltx_p">The ability to translate unknown embeddings into a different space while preserving their geometry has serious implications for security. An adversary with access to a database of only embedding vectors can extract sensitive information about underlying documents, sufficient for classification and attribute inference.</p>
  
</div>
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2505.12540v4/universal2.svg" id="S0.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/153;" width="381" height="153"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S0.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S0.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Left: input embeddings from different model families (T5-based GTR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite> and BERT-based GTE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>) are fundamentally incomparable. Right:
given unpaired embedding samples from different models on different texts, our model learns a latent representation where they are closely aligned.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S0.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.12540v4/diagram.png" id="S0.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/179;" width="405" height="179" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S0.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S0.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Given only a vector database from an unknown model, <span id="S0.F2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> translates the database into the space of a known model using latent structure alone. Converted embeddings reveal sensitive information about the original documents, such as the topic of an email (pictured, real example).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Text embeddings are the backbone of modern NLP, powering tasks like retrieval, RAG, classification, and clustering. There are many embedding models trained on different datasets, data shufflings, and initializations. An embedding of a text encodes its semantics: a good model maps texts with similar semantics to vectors close to each other in the embedding space. Since semantics is a property of text, different embeddings of the same text should encode the same semantics. In practice, however, different models encode texts into completely different and incompatible vector spaces.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Platonic Representation Hypothesis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> conjectures that all vision models of sufficient size converge to the same latent representation. We propose a stronger, constructive version of this hypothesis for text models: the universal latent structure of text representations can be learned and, furthermore, harnessed to translate representations from one space to another without any paired data or encoders.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we show that the Strong Platonic Representation Hypothesis holds in practice. Given unpaired examples of embeddings from two models with different architectures and training data, our method learns a latent representation in which the embeddings are almost identical (<a href="#S0.F1" title="In Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We draw inspiration from research on aligning word embeddings across languages <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx62" title="" class="ltx_ref">62</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> and unsupervised image translation
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx70" title="" class="ltx_ref">70</a>]</cite>. Our <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> method uses adversarial losses and cycle consistency to learn to encode embeddings into a shared latent space and decode with minimal loss. This makes unsupervised translation possible. We use a basic adversarial approach with vector space preservation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> to learn a mapping from an unknown embedding distribution to a known one.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> is the
<span id="S1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">first method to successfully translate embeddings from the space of one model to another without paired data.<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note"><span id="footnote1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">1</span></span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <span id="footnote1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">Prior work has successfully translated </span><em id="footnote1.11" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_medium ltx_font_italic">word</em><span id="footnote1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> embeddings between languages, typically relying on overlapping vocabularies across languages. In contrast, we translate embeddings of entire sequences between model spaces.</span></span></span></span></span>
<span id="S1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span>
translations achieve cosine similarity as high as <math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.96</annotation></semantics></math> to the ground-truth vectors in their target embedding spaces and perfect matching on over <math id="S1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8000</annotation></semantics></math> shuffled embeddings (without access to the set of possible matches in advance).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To show that our translations preserve not only the relative geometry of embeddings but also the semantics of underlying inputs, we extract information from them using zero-shot attribute inference and inversion, without any knowledge of the model that produced the original embeddings.<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          Our code is available <a href="https://github.com/rjha18/vec2vec/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">on GitHub.</a></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Problem formulation: unsupervised embedding translation</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Consider a collection of embedding vectors <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{u_{1},\ldots u_{n}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{u_{1},\ldots u_{n}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, for example, a dump of a compromised vector database, where each <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{i}=M_{1}(d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{i}=M_{1}(d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> is generated by an unknown encoder <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}:\mathbb{V}^{s}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d_{M_{1}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝕍</mi><mi>s</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}:\mathbb{V}^{s}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d_{M_{1}}}</annotation></semantics></math> from an unknown document <math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. We cannot make queries to <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and do not know its training data, nor architectural details. Our goal is to extract any information about the documents <math id="S2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.12540v4/spaces.png" id="S2.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/159;" width="429" height="159" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S2.F3.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Unsupervised embedding translation<span id="S2.F3.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">. With access to only <math id="S2.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{i}=M_{1}(d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{i}=M_{1}(d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="S2.F3.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> seeks to generate a translation <math id="S2.F3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(u_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(u_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> that is close in <math id="S2.F3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>’s embedding space to the ideal embedding <math id="S2.F3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}=M_{2}(d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}=M_{2}(d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> without access to <math id="S2.F3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.F3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math id="S2.F3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We do assume access to a different encoder <math id="S2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> that we can query at will to generate new embeddings in some other space. We also assume high-level distributional knowledge about the hidden documents: their modality (text) and language (e.g., English). To extract information, we may translate <math id="S2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{u_{1},\ldots u_{n}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{u_{1},\ldots u_{n}\}</annotation></semantics></math> into the output space of <math id="S2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and apply techniques like inversion that require the encoder.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Limitations of correspondence methods.</span>
There is significant prior research on the problem of <span id="S2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">matching</span> or <span id="S2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">correspondence</span> between sets of embedding vectors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx54" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>]</cite>. These methods typically assume that the two (or more) sets of embeddings are generated by different encoders on the <em id="S2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">same or highly-overlapping inputs</em>. In other words, for each unknown vector, there must already exist a set of candidate vectors in a different embedding. In practice, it is unrealistic to expect that such a database be available, so these methods are not directly applicable. Some matching methods, however, support translation between embedding spaces without overlapping inputs. Our experiments demonstrate that these methods struggle significantly, even when correspondence exists.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Our task is inherently more challenging than matching, because we do not assume access to encoder <math id="S2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, nor do we have additional representations of documents <math id="S2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{d_{1},\ldots,d_{n}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{d_{1},\ldots,d_{n}}</annotation></semantics></math> beyond their embeddings <math id="S2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{i}=M_{1}(d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{i}=M_{1}(d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, we rely solely on unsupervised <span id="S2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">translation</span> from <math id="S2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The effectiveness of such unsupervised translation approaches thus critically depends on identifying and leveraging shared geometric structures within the embedding spaces produced by <math id="S2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Strong Platonic Representation Hypothesis.</span>
Our hope that unsupervised embedding translation is possible at all rests on the stronger version of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. Our conjecture is as follows:
<em id="S2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">neural networks trained with the same objective and modality, but with different data and model architectures, converge to a universal latent space such that a translation between their respective representations can be learned without any pairwise correspondence.</em></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Translation enables information extraction.</span> Solving unsupervised translation will allow us to use information extraction tools designed to operate on vectors produced by known encoders. For example, we could apply inversion models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx67" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite> to recover unknown documents <math id="S2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{d_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{d_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Our method: <span id="S3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span></h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unsupervised translation has been successful in computer vision, using a combination of cycle consistency and adversarial regularization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx70" title="" class="ltx_ref">70</a>]</cite>. Our design of <span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> is inspired in part by these methods. We aim to learn embedding-space translations that are cycle-consistent (mapping to and from an embedding space should end in the same place) and indistinguishable (embeddings for the same text from either space should have identical latents).</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Architecture</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose a modular architecture, where embeddings are encoded and decoded using space-specific adapter modules and passed through a shared backbone network. <a href="#S0.F2" title="In Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows these components. Input adapters <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{1}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{1}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{2}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{2}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> transform embeddings from each encoder-specific space into a universal latent representation of dimension <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>. The shared backbone <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T:\mathbb{R}^{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T:\mathbb{R}^{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> extracts a common latent embedding from adapted inputs. Output adapters <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{1}:\mathbb{R}^{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{1}:\mathbb{R}^{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{2}:\mathbb{R}^{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>Z</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{2}:\mathbb{R}^{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> translate these common latent embeddings back into the encoder-specific spaces. Thus, translation functions <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1},F_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1},F_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and additional reconstruction mappings <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{1},R_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{1},R_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined as:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}=B_{2}\circ T\circ A_{1},\quad F_{2}=B_{1}\circ T\circ A_{2}\quad R_{1}=B_{1}\circ T\circ A_{1}\quad R_{2}=B_{2}\circ T\circ A_{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}=B_{2}\circ T\circ A_{1},\quad F_{2}=B_{1}\circ T\circ A_{2}\quad R_{1}=B_{1}\circ T\circ A_{1}\quad R_{2}=B_{2}\circ T\circ A_{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Parameters of all components are collectively denoted <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\{A_{1},A_{2},T,B_{1},B_{2}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\{A_{1},A_{2},T,B_{1},B_{2}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike images, embeddings do not have any spatial bias. Instead of CNNs, we use multilayer perceptrons (MLP) with residual connections, layer normalization, and SiLU nonlinearities. Discriminators mirror this structure but omit residual connections to simplify adversarial learning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Optimization</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to the ‘generator’ networks <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>, we introduce discriminators operating on both the latent representations of <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>) and the output embeddings (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{1},D_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1},D_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our goal is to train the parameters of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> by solving:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{*}=\arg\min_{\theta}\max_{D_{1},D_{2},D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}}(F_{1},F_{2},D_{1},D_{2},D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell})+\lambda_{\text{gen}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}(\theta)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mi>θ</mi></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>adv</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>gen</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>gen</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{*}=\arg\min_{\theta}\max_{D_{1},D_{2},D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}}(F_{1},F_{2},D_{1},D_{2},D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell})+\lambda_{\text{gen}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}(\theta),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>adv</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>gen</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}</annotation></semantics></math> represent adversarial and generator-specific constraints respectively and hyperparameter <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\rm gen}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>gen</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\rm gen}</annotation></semantics></math> controls their tradeoff.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adversarial.</span>
The adversarial loss encourages generated embeddings to match the empirical distributions of original embeddings both at the embedding and latent levels. Specifically, applying the standard GAN loss formulation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> to both levels yields:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}}(F_{1},F_{2},D_{1},D_{2},D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>adv</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}}(F_{1},F_{2},D_{1},D_{2},D_{1}^{\ell},D_{2}^{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{1},F_{1})+\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{2},F_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>GAN</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>GAN</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{1},F_{1})+\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{2},F_{2})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\quad+\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{1}^{\ell},T\circ A_{1})+\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{2}^{\ell},T\circ A_{2})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>GAN</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>GAN</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\quad+\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{1}^{\ell},T\circ A_{1})+\mathcal{L}_{\text{GAN}}(D_{2}^{\ell},T\circ A_{2}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Generator.</span>
Because adversarial losses alone do not guarantee that translated embeddings preserve semantics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx70" title="" class="ltx_ref">70</a>]</cite>, we introduce three additional constraints to help the generator learn a useful mapping:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Reconstruction</span> enforces that an embedding, when mapped into the latent space and back into its original embedding space, closely matches its initial representation:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}(R_{1},R_{2})=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p}\|R_{1}(x)-x\|_{2}^{2}+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim q}\|R_{2}(y)-y\|_{2}^{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}(R_{1},R_{2})=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p}\|R_{1}(x)-x\|_{2}^{2}+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim q}\|R_{2}(y)-y\|_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> are distributions of embeddings sampled from <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Cycle-consistency</span> acts as an unsupervised proxy for supervised pair alignment, ensuring that <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> can translate an embedding to the other embedding space and back again with minimal corruption:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{CC}}(F_{1},F_{2})=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p}\|F_{2}(F_{1}(x))-x\|_{2}^{2}+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim q}\|F_{1}(F_{2}(y))-y\|_{2}^{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>CC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{CC}}(F_{1},F_{2})=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p}\|F_{2}(F_{1}(x))-x\|_{2}^{2}+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim q}\|F_{1}(F_{2}(y))-y\|_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vector space preservation (VSP)</span> ensures that pairwise relationships between translated embeddings are consistent with the target space <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx65" title="" class="ltx_ref">65</a>]</cite>. Given a batch of <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> embeddings <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1},...,x_{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1},...,x_{B}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{1},...,y_{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1},...,y_{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, we sum their average pairwise distances after translation by both <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{VSP}}(F_{1},F_{2})=\frac{1}{B^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{B}\sum_{j=1}^{B}\bigg[" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>VSP</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></munderover></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></munderover></mstyle><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">[</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{VSP}}(F_{1},F_{2})=\frac{1}{B^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{B}\sum_{j=1}^{B}\bigg[</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\|M_{1}(x_{i})\cdot M_{1}(x_{j})-F_{2}(M_{2}(y_{i}))\cdot F_{2}(M_{2}(y_{j}))\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\|M_{1}(x_{i})\cdot M_{1}(x_{j})-F_{2}(M_{2}(y_{i}))\cdot F_{2}(M_{2}(y_{j}))\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle+\|M_{2}(y_{i})\cdot M_{2}(y_{j})-F_{1}(M_{1}(x_{i}))\cdot F_{1}(M_{1}(x_{j}))\|_{2}^{2}\bigg]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">+</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+\|M_{2}(y_{i})\cdot M_{2}(y_{j})-F_{1}(M_{1}(x_{i}))\cdot F_{1}(M_{1}(x_{j}))\|_{2}^{2}\bigg]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Combining these losses yields:
<math id="S3.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}(\theta)=\lambda_{\text{rec}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}(R_{1},R_{2})+\lambda_{\text{CC}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{CC}}(F_{1},F_{2})+\lambda_{\text{VSP}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{VSP}}(F_{1},F_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>gen</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>CC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>CC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>VSP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>VSP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}(\theta)=\lambda_{\text{rec}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}(R_{1},R_{2})+\lambda_{\text{CC}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{CC}}(F_{1},F_{2})+\lambda_{\text{VSP}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{VSP}}(F_{1},F_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, where hyperparameters <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{CC}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>CC</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{CC}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{rec}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{rec}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{VSP}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>VSP</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{VSP}}</annotation></semantics></math> control relative importance.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experimental setup</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Preliminaries</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Datasets.</span>
We use the <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Natural Questions (NQ)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> dataset of user queries and Wikipedia-sourced answers for training (a <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-million subset) and evaluation (a <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65536" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>65536</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65536</annotation></semantics></math> subset). To evaluate information extraction, we use
<span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">TweetTopic</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, a dataset of tweets multi-labeled by 19 topics; a random <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math>-record subset of
<span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Pseudo Re-identified MIMIC-III (MIMIC)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>, a pseudo re-identified version of the MIMIC dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite> of patient records multi-labeled by 2673 MedCAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite> disease descriptions; and a random <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math>-email subset of
the <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Enron Email Corpus (Enron)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>, an unlabeled, public dataset of
internal emails from a defunct energy company. In <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Text-image retrieval on MS COCO ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>, we ablate a model on <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">MS COCO</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, a captioned image dataset, to evaluate performance on multimodal retrieval.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Models.</span> <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.1 Preliminaries ‣ 4 Experimental setup ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> lists the embedding models representing four size categories, five transformer backbones, and two output dimensionalities. Granite is multilingual; CLIP is multimodal. Since Qwen is very compute-intensive, we only evaluate it for a single model pair in <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Translating to and from Qwen ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S4.T1.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S4.T1.3.1" class="ltx_tr">

<th id="S4.T1.3.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T1.3.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Backbone</span></th>
<th id="S4.T1.3.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T1.3.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Year</span></th>
<th id="S4.T1.3.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T1.3.1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Dims</span></th>

</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S4.T1.3.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T1.3.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S4.T1.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">[</span><a href="#bib.bibx47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a><span id="S4.T1.3.2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">]</span></cite><span id="S4.T1.3.2.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">  gtr</span></th>
<th id="S4.T1.3.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T1.3.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">110</span></th>
<th id="S4.T1.3.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T1.3.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">T5</span></th>
<td id="S4.T1.3.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T1.3.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">2021</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.3.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T1.3.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">768</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.3.2.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T1.3.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">512</span></td></tr>
