</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:70%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A4.T9.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:129%;">Table 9</span>: </span><span id="A4.T9.10" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:129%;">Cross-model text-image retrieval on MS COCO: granite <math id="A4.T9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> clip <span id="A4.T9.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> trained on NQ (unimodal) and evaluated on MS COCO’s validation set. The rank metric varies from 1 to 5000, thus 2500 corresponds to a random ordering. Queries (captions) embedded with either Granite or CLIP. Documents (images) embedded with CLIP. Each caption has a unique image. Standard errors are shown in parentheses.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our <span id="A4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span>s can “stitch" modalities onto unimodal models by translating to a multimodal model. To test this, we evaluated cross-modal text-image retrieval on MS COCO’s validation set (5000 examples) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, translating queries (captions) embedded with Granite to retrieve documents (images) embedded with CLIP using our unimodal granite <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> clip translator from <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Evaluating information extraction ‣ 4 Experimental setup ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>. Each caption has a unique image. We report Recall@16, cosine similarities, and Rank, with CLIP (for both documents and queries) as our baseline.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As <a href="#A4.T9" title="In Appendix D Text-image retrieval on MS COCO ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows, translating Granite embeddings to CLIP enables non-negligible cross-model multimodal retrieval with <span id="A4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">a unimodal model for queries</span>—despite zero multimodal training. Further evaluation of this paradigm with multimodal-specific training is a promising direction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Initialization robustness by model backbone</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GAN training is notoriously unstable to weight initialization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx53" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>]</cite>. To measure our method’s robustness, we trained fifteen e5 <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> gte (shared backbone) and e5 <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> gtr (cross-backbone) <span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span>s on the NQ dataset for a fixed 10 epochs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For the translations between related models, <span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> training was relatively stable across random seeds: 14 out of 15 seeds achieved at least 80% top-1 accuracy within a fixed epoch budget, while the remaining run reached 72%. In contrast, translation between unrelated models proved significantly less stable, with only 3 out of 15 runs achieving convergence (80% top-1 accuracy). We leave improving the seed stability of our training regime as future, valuable work.</p>
</div>
</section>

The rank metric varies from 1 to 800, thus 400 corresponds to a random ordering. Standard errors are shown in parentheses. Symbols denote the lowest-rank solver: Earth Mover’s Distance<sup id="A6.T10.12.2" class="ltx_sup">∗</sup> and Gromov-Wasserstein<sup id="A6.T10.12.3" class="ltx_sup">‡</sup></span></figcaption>

The rank metric varies from 1 to 8192, thus 4096 corresponds to a random ordering. Standard errors are shown in parentheses. Symbols denote the lowest-rank solver: Earth Mover’s Distance<sup id="A6.T11.14.2" class="ltx_sup">∗</sup>, Sinkhorn<sup id="A6.T11.14.3" class="ltx_sup">†</sup> and Gromov-Wasserstein<sup id="A6.T11.14.4" class="ltx_sup">‡</sup></span></figcaption>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Zero-shot inversion on TweetTopic</h2>

<figure id="A7.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.12540v4/tweettopic_heatmap.png" id="A7.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:238/213;" width="238" height="213" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A7.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A7.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Leakage of information via inversion. Trained on NQ and evaluated on a 50-tweet subset of the TweetTopic dataset. Cells denote judge accuracy.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We replicate <a href="#S6.F5" title="In 6 Using vec2vec translations to extract information ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> on the TweetTopic dataset in <a href="#A7.F7" title="In Appendix G Zero-shot inversion on TweetTopic ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, extracting information given <span id="A7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">only</span> translated embeddings of tweets. We achieve non-negligible leakage for all model pairs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Prompt for measuring information extraction</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S6.F5" title="In 6 Using vec2vec translations to extract information ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and <a href="#A7.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix G Zero-shot inversion on TweetTopic ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> utilize an LLM judge to determine whether the approximate inversion (using <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx67" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>) of a translated email embedding leaks information about the original email. <a href="#A8.F8" title="In Appendix H Prompt for measuring information extraction ‣ Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows our prompt to the GPT-4o judge:</p>
</div>

    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"

      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
